17.1: And he answered Edomyas and Amalek: "God, whose is the judgment of heaven and earth, shall not rule over them; into his hand he hath trodden the house of his sanctuary, for they are a foreign people who walk not in righteousness."
17.2: And there is no fear of God before their eyes; for [they stop at] no lewdness, nor the shedding of blood, nor the eating of sacrifices, and abominable things, and carrion, nor aught that is like unto these — reprobates and gəmunanə.
17.3: They have no faith, and no salt; for they are haters of good, and they know not God; and the way of peace which was laid — and affliction, and every unclean deed, and hukätä, and zäfänä, and täwənetä — as their father Säbəlyanos taught them.

18.1: Remember how thou didst come unto God, and all was in His hand; and stand thou firm in the work which thou hast done, that thou mayest stand before Him.
18.2: For so are the giant children — evil and wicked — and there is none strong nor mighty among them; and their stature, and the greatness of their seed; and they set not God before them, and know not that He is their Maker, who brought them from where they were not.
18.3: But as for their fathers — while they were angels, they sang with the angels in the heavens; but when they sinned, their lust, and they went down into the punishment of judgment for ever.
18.4: And they took wives from the daughters of men, for God made for them flesh like that of men, that He might bring them into bondage through the pride of their heart, and reprove them, if they kept the commandment and the law.
18.5: But as for them, they kept not the commandment, and He brought them down into the judgment of burning fire, with Diyabolos their father; and because of them the days were shortened for man, for God changed them — the angels who had sinned — into men.
18.6: And he led astray the children of men with them, and brought them down into Sheol, in their judgment.
18.7: But in former time, the days of man — when they, unto 120 years — for the days of man were shortened, because the angels sinned with the daughters of Qayəl.
18.8: And God said: "My spirit shall not abide in them, for they are flesh and blood."
18.9: And therefore our days are shortened; and moreover there are those who die while they are babes, for few are our days beside our fathers', because of our sins and our iniquities.
18.10: But as for our fathers, long were their days, for they kept the commandment, and turned not from God.
18.11: And they instructed their children, that they might teach them; and they instructed their offspring, that they should not transgress the commandment of God.
18.12: And therefore long were their days in righteousness, because they transgressed not the commandment of God, with their children and their offspring.

19.1: And when the children of Cain multiplied, they made harps and timbrels and psalteries and bəʿəza, and all täwənetä and zäfänä.
19.2: And again there were born children to Cain — good and polluted — from the wife of Abel the righteous, whom he killed for her sake, for polluted was she; and after he killed his brother, he took [a wife] there, and ʾəntakətəni was she.
19.3: And he married from his father's [house] — he took his [wife] there — into the desert of Qefaz, by the road of ʿArab; and her children, the polluted ones, who became polluted like ʾAmon.
19.4: And therefore the angels descended unto the children of Cain, and they tarried not a single hour, and they took wives for themselves, whom they chose.
19.5: And therefore God was angry with us and with them, for together we were led astray into error with them because of their sins.
19.6: And Diyabolos also led astray our father Adam and our mother Eve into his error, while he deceived them and said to them: "Ye shall be gods, like God your Maker."
19.7: But as for them, in their they believed, and transgressed the commandment of their Maker, who brought them forth from nothingness, that they might bow down and praise His holy name.
19.8: But as for them who despised the gift of God for themselves — He, their Lord, forsook them; and unto Him.
19.9: As David saith: "In his pride the sinner scorneth the poor; for through the pride of Diyabolos, Adam — [who had been] established in the judgment of righteousness before God his God — [fell].
19.10: And likewise we — [like] the angels who sinned with the daughters of Qayəl — were led astray into their error; and therefore our days are shortened from the days of our fathers, which God gave us.
19.11: But as for them, they did good, and there is nought whereby evil may come nigh them, for they made firm their hearts toward God, and they teach their children and their offspring, that they depart not from the commandment of God which He taught them.
19.12: But as for them, if they do [good], yet tell not their children, and teach them not, there is none who shall them.
19.13: As David saith: "And they hid not from their children unto the [next] generation, but told the praises of God — His might and His wonders which He wrought — that they might teach their children, that they might and do [good], and keep His judgment unto God, and that they might keep the commandment, as their fathers who kept [it] unto God in the śənä of their deeds."
19.14: And they forsook not the commandment which their fathers kept for them, when the fear of God came upon them, nor His judgment — even as they were taught by their fathers.
19.15: And their children also were taught by their fathers, that they might their gəʿəzomu, and praise to their Maker, for they kept the commandment and loved Him.
19.16: And He heareth their prayer, and hideth not Himself from them; but as for Him, He is merciful.
19.17: Abundant is His, and He executeth not with all His punishments.

20.1: Remember, my brethren, and forget not what the ancients told you: how God will keep the righteousness of them that do good.
20.2: And their fruit shall be multiplied upon the earth, and their remembrance shall be for good for ever; and their seed shall not be cut off from upon the earth.
20.3: And He shall deliver them from the hand of all their oppressors and their enemies who pursue them; for on their account it shall come to pass unto them, and He will not abandon them into the hand of their enemies.
20.4: And He shall be unto them a helper in their tribulation — unto them that love His name; and they shall be kept, and He will forgive them all their sins.

21.1: David trusted in God, and He was his helper; for he trusted in Him, and He delivered him from the hand of Saul the king.
21.2: And from Absalom his son, and from the ʾElofəlawəyanə, and from the Amalekites and the Edomites, and from the Qärənewonə — yea, from all these that rose up against him — God delivered David, for he trusted in Him and kept His law.
21.3: But as for them that trusted not in Him — the evil kings — God delivered them not, for they were given over into the hand of their enemies, for cut off from God is he.
21.4: Hezekiah trusted in God, and He delivered him from the hand of the great Syrian.
21.5: But Manasseh his son was given over into the hand of his enemy, for he set not his trust in God. And as for them that gave Manasseh over to his enemy — it was not [done] thus, but they bound him and carried him into their land; for he set not his trust upon God, and feared not Him who made him and exalted him and made him great.
21.6: And therefore he was held back from the gift which had been given him, for he directed not his way unto God his God — that his days might be at rest, and that his enemy might rise against him, and that there might be strength and might and fəṣəmä and käwalä.
21.7: For better is trust in God than many hosts, and [better] than trust in horses and chariots and bows.
21.8: For he that trusteth in Him, in God, shall live and be honoured and be exalted exceedingly.
21.9: But as for them that trusted not in God, and trusted in much wealth — they became estranged from His grace which He had given them; for God is no respecter of persons.
21.10: But as for them that trusted in Him, He will keep them; and as for them that serve Him, He will put them in [His] service — and their help shall not be slow in their tribulation, when their enemies rise up against them; for they set not their hearts on His will unto God, but kept His commandments unto God.
21.11: And he that is firm in the will of God, and in the will of His commandments, and keepeth His law — unto him He shall be a helper in his tribulation.
21.12: And what shall they say of him that trusteth not in God? He is not better than the beasts that perish in the earth — he that is puffed up in his heart and exalteth himself against his God, yea, against his Maker.
21.13: And what is man's pride? His glory passeth away, and his exaltation, and his honour, and his riches.
21.14: And his trust shall not save his pride from death; for He that made him is God, and it is He that is his Maker.
21.15: And let them that trust in God keep His law; and let them that keep His law keep His commandments; and let them that keep His commandments keep His judgments — for their enemies shall fear Him, and they shall fear His will; for He that is with Him shall not be ashamed.
21.16: And let them that trust in God keep His commandments; and let them that keep His commandments, that they keep His judgments — and let the commandment fear Him and His will; and the law is theirs.
21.17: And he that loveth God keepeth His commandments; and he that loveth God, let the servant love the Son; and he that loveth his father loveth him whom he begat.
21.18: And what man is as the man of God — the man that God, that He maketh him to dwell in His good place; and in the midst of the garden He planted him, and He made him, and He set him, and He gave him to eat?
21.19: And what shall they say of them that trust not in God? God shall make His face shine upon the righteous
21.20: But as for them that trust not in God — why do they trust in the gods, and [why do] they not receive the grace of the kingdom?
21.21: For they trust in the counsel of men, that they may cut off the grace of God; but God will not give them the grace of His kingdom.
21.22: And therefore is it said, "Let them that trust in the Lord dwell in the good land," for He feedeth them with much wealth.
21.23: And therefore the righteous are exalted over all the earth; and therefore do they bring forth the fruit of righteousness, and their seed is blessed, for God loveth the righteous.
21.24: And as for them that trust in Him, He bringeth them low and lifteth them up
21.25: And therefore let them that trust in God fear Him and keep His law; for their enemies shall be delivered into their hands.
21.27: But as for them that trust not in God — He shall not have mercy upon them, and they shall receive their reward from their enemies.

21.29: And he that trusteth in Him, in God — blessed is the man that trusteth in Him.

22.1: Remember — behold — the names of them that do good, and forget not their deeds.
22.2: And be zealous, that thy name may be as the name of their fathers — that in heaven thou mayest rejoice with them in the dwelling of light, which He prepared for the elect, [for] kings and princes that did the will of God.
22.3: Again, know thou and learn the names of the evil kings and princes — that they may be punished and put to shame among men after their death.
22.4: Who in heaven shall be punished with the wicked and the ʿalawəyanə — that did not the will of God; for though they see and hear, they make not their way straight.
22.5: But thou, go not in the way of the wicked, whom God rejected because of the evil of their deeds; but be thou elect, and integrity and uprightness.
22.6: And open unto righteousness, and justify the poor and the dying; and deliver [them] from the hand of them that oppress them — the sinners.
22.7: And stand for the dying as a father, that thou mayest deliver him from the hand of him that oppresseth him; and dread [shall fall] when he is cut off from among the dying in thy midst — that thou be not afraid in the sea of fire, wherein are punished the sinners that repented not.
22.8: Make straight thy steps in the way of peace, and seek peace, and follow after it — for the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and His ears unto their supplications.
22.9: Be holy unto the LORD against them that do evil, that He may root out their memorial from the earth; and there shall not remain of them any that is left — neither in the wilderness, nor in ʿarəfət.
22.10: And I will not turn away My face, until I destroy them that keep not My word — for I am a jealous God, who repayeth them that hate Me, and them that keep not My word.
22.11: And I will honour them that honour Me, and keep My word.

24.12: And they are not ashamed before the man that seeth them, nor before him that rebuketh them, nor before the elder; and when they hear of the goods of the world, they forget that which their eyes have not seen, and when they have seen with their eyes, it seemeth unto them what they have uttered with their mouths; for the fear of God is not before their eyes.
24.13: And their rulers also take counsel with fornicators; and what they have spoken in the morning, they undo in the evening; for they are liars, and there is no uprightness in their mouths.
24.14: And their kings also, the crafty, run unto evil; for they oppress the poor and needy, and they drive them not to the stranger from the hand of them that oppress them.
24.15: And therefore there shall be no kings that are; but they shall unto the stranger and unto.
24.16: But they are the murderers and the proud, who drink blood, and have no mercy, like a mother, and a bird like its young; for narrow is all their way that they have seen, and that which is theirs they forget.
24.17: And they have no mercy on the poor and the stranger; but they love to gather unto themselves, and seize the goods of their masters by violence; and all that they find they heap up, that they may store it in their treasuries, and rejoice therein.
24.18: Woe unto their souls, when God shall take them in His anger; because they established not their ordinance in their life; for they shall be suddenly extinguished, as he that goeth forth to the way and findeth nothing, and bringeth nothing into his house.
24.19: And likewise they shall be extinguished in the land in one, when God rebuketh them; they shall perish in their time. For God hasteneth not to quench him, but waiteth until he enter into repentance.
24.20: But if he enter not into repentance, God shall quench them, as of old them that were before them, who kept not the commandment of God in purity.
24.21: And the fornicators, the flesh of man, and the drinkers of blood — and the fear of God is not in them at any time; for quickly they pass unto the, when they rise from their, and they rest not from the work of iniquity.
24.22: Of fornication and drink and in evil, and ḫagwələ — that they may destroy many souls upon the earth.

25.1: I say unto their souls: when I seize them in Mine anger, saith the Lord, whom all obey; for perverse is their way, and all that walk in the way of Satan are destroyed.
25.2: And the way of God they know not, and they have turned their backs, and turned away from the law.
25.3: And I will recompense them according to the evil of their works, afterward in the day of judgment; I will visit them, as it is written: I have kept the evil of their works, and they shall not escape from My hand; for I am the Lord, who killeth and maketh alive, who rebuketh and pardoneth.
25.4: And there is none that escapeth from My hand, neither under the earth, nor above the heavens, nor in the sea, nor in the depths of the waters; for I am the Lord, from the end unto the ends of the world, and every soul is in My hand.
25.5: He commanded under the earth, and to the fishes in the midst of the sea, and to the birds in the midst of the air, and to the in the wilderness, from the end unto the end, and unto the ends of the world — this is He.
